test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements are true based on the 4NH₃ (g)+5O₂ (g)→4NO(g)+6H2O(g)?

(a) N gets oxidized.

(b) O gets oxidized.

(c) N gets reduced.

(d) O gets reduced.
solution:
The correct answer is __**(a) and (d)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the given reaction, nitrogen (N) in NH₃ goes from -3 oxidation state to +2 oxidation state in NO, which indicates oxidation (loss of electrons).
 
• Oxygen (O) in O₂ goes from 0 oxidation state to -2 oxidation state in H₂O, which indicates reduction (gain of electrons).
 
• Since nitrogen is being oxidized and oxygen is being reduced, statements (a) and (d) are true.
 
• The other statements (b) and (c) are incorrect as they contradict the changes in oxidation states observed in the reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• Oxidation is the process where an atom, ion, or molecule loses electrons, leading to an increase in its oxidation state.
 
• In the given reaction, nitrogen in NH₃ (oxidation state -3) is oxidized to NO (oxidation state +2).
 
 
 
• **Reduction:**
 
 
• Reduction is the process where an atom, ion, or molecule gains electrons, leading to a decrease in its oxidation state.
 
• In the given reaction, oxygen in O₂ (oxidation state 0) is reduced to H₂O (oxidation state -2).
 
 
 
• **Oxidation State:**
 
 
• The oxidation state, or oxidation number, is a measure of the degree of oxidation of an atom in a substance.
 
• It is a hypothetical charge that an atom would have if all bonds to atoms of different elements were 100% ionic.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reaction:**
 
 
• A redox (reduction-oxidation) reaction is a type of chemical reaction that involves a transfer of electrons between two species.
 
• It consists of two half-reactions: oxidation (loss of electrons) and reduction (gain of electrons).
